newsitem.title: UK: Sikh separatist to be freed from British prison.
newsitem.headline: Sikh separatist to be freed from British prison.

text.p: A Sikh independence campaigner held in a British prison for six years is to be released after winning the final round in a battle against deportation on Friday.

British Home Secretary (interior minister) Michael Howard authorised the release of Karamjit Singh Chahal after the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg rejected the British government's bid to expel him.
The court backed Chahal's case that he faced torture and possibly death if sent home to India and that such a prospect was a breach of his human rights.
Chahal has been battling to avoid deportation from prison where he has spent six years and three months without charge and without being told of any alleged offences.
He was originally held under suspicion of being a separatist guerrilla, involved in the Sikh campaign for an independent homeland in Khalistan.
But the Strasbourg judges decided that Britain had failed to demonstrate Chahal was a national security risk.
